doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Current work with Conte, Hall of Fame and college workshops
summary: Pete describes the Brothers, their CD, the Jazz Hall of Fame induction and coming concerts.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s your playing routine these days?

Well Conte and I have been doing very well together as The Brothers, in fact we’ve got a CD coming out and we were both fortunate to be inducted in the National Jazz Hall of Fame which was nice, with some good company. Nat Cole’s wife was there posthumously picking up a trophy for him and a lot of people, Chet Baker, that had been inducted. And that’s done a lot for us as The Brothers – we’re finally coming out with, we’ve done it already, it will be released by Hindsight Records, they just released an album done by SuperSax in Japan, they got a hold of that. They pulled out choice things I think. They’re very particular who they release. So that plus the concerts we’re doing, we’ll be going to, not Phoenix, Scottsdale, that’s where the next one is being held in May, the new winners to be inducted in the Jazz Hall of Fame, and it’s a three day affair, black tie type of thing. I think Clint Eastwood was going to emcee one of them, I don’t know, maybe this one. And so that’s one thing. Then we’re doing different colleges which we do — we’ve done Lionel Hampton’s School of Music three or four times together. We’re not doing it this February. We’ll be doing a ship, we’re booked on a ship for six days which we’ll take our own rhythm section, Conte and I, and then we’re playing some college, Imperial College, right near the border, east of San Diego, and we’ll be doing a one night concert there, and I think Conte and I will give a seminar to the music department.
You seem to have played right through the rock & roll revolution, intact.

Very lucky. I think that’s when I did most of the work in the studio, then branched out for a hit and a miss every now and then, and then we were very lucky with Alabama and Chicago, they asked us to dub on like several years ago, if we could overdub some things.
